alg: Before the attempt submit the number of puzzles to attempt, at least 2, and that number cannot be changed afterwards.
Attempting fewer than 6 puzzles gives a time limit of 10 minutes times the number of puzzles, otherwise the limit is 60 minutes.
Rankings are assessed by puzzles solved minus puzzles not solved, greater difference is better, e.g. 4/5 counts as 3 points.
Times are measured and truncated to seconds, and the judge records puzzles solved, puzzles attempted, and the final time.
All cubes are memorized in one look, then solved blindfolded. The event reuses the 3BLD solving methods, one cube at a time.
Memorize the sticker locations directly, in order, with no association system. Tapping means touching the stickers in order in groups of 2 to 4 until the sequence sticks.
Assign each sticker one letter of a fixed scheme, Speffz is the standard, then memorize the cycle letters. A lone letter at the end signals parity.
Combine 2 letters into one image, an object animal or person, place the images along a journey so the order is recallable, e.g. QU SR NX IV PR DE as QUick StaR NeXus IVy PRint DEad.

Turn 2 letters into one sound, monosyllables, filler vowels between consonants, e.g. TN = tin, F-O R-D G-E L-R reads foe rod gee ler. Fast but short lived, so memo it last and execute it first, or use it for one orbit such as corners.
Words not meant to be visualized, used to build sentences, e.g. TH = the.
The original Pochmann scheme: each edge pair of colors becomes a memorable object, e.g. Red-Blue is Spiderman.
Assign numbers to positions, hexadecimal with bits for orientation works for corner and edge permutations.
A fixed journey of locations acts as the background, each location holds one or more memo images, the route preserves the order across many cubes.
Person Action Object: each sticker maps to a person an action and an object, 6 letters compress to about 4 images, e.g. J K E T O R = a JoKer EaTing an OReo.
